compatibility.title: Which Land Rover Models Use the Puma 2.2 TDCi?
compatibility.intro: The Puma 2.2 TDCi was the final diesel engine fitted to the classic Land Rover Defender (L316) before its production ended in 2016. Introduced to meet Euro 5 emissions standards, it replaced the earlier 2.4-litre Puma unit, offering improved refinement, a revised 6-speed gearbox, and better fuel economy while retaining the Defender's legendary off-road capability.

failures.title: Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal or external leaks, leading to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential engine overheating if ignored. This is often exacerbated by carbon buildup in the intake system.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard maintenance fix. However, if the leak has caused severe overheating, the cylinder head may be compromised, necessitating a full engine replacement. Read our full coolant system failure guide.

items.title: Turbocharger Actuator Failure
items.whatHappens: The turbo actuator arm can seize or fail, leading to a loss of boost, reduced power, and an illuminated engine management light. This is a common wear item on the 2.2-litre Duratorq architecture.
items.repairVsReplace: Actuator replacement or turbo refurbishment is a standard repair and does not typically require a full engine replacement unless turbo debris has entered the oil system and caused bearing damage.

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: The timing chain tensioner can wear over time, leading to chain slap and a distinct rattling noise on cold startup. While less catastrophic than the timing issues seen in the earlier Td5 or later Ingenium engines, it still requires prompt attention to prevent long-term wear.
items.repairVsReplace: Tensioner and chain replacement is a viable repair. If caught early, it prevents the need for a full Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The Puma 2.2 TDCi is generally considered more refined and reliable than the preceding 2.4-litre Puma engine, with fewer catastrophic bottom-end failures, provided the EGR and turbo systems are proactively maintained .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Puma 2.2 TDCi
variants.intro: The Puma 2.2 TDCi is a specific 2.2-litre iteration of the Ford-sourced Duratorq diesel family. Confirming your exact code is critical because, while it shares core architecture with the Freelander 2 and Evoque (224DT), the Defender-specific calibration, mounting, and ancillary setups differ significantly. WHERE TO FIND THE CODE: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, usually visible near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It will also be explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Code" or "Engine Capacity", and can be decoded directly from your 17-character VIN. COMMONLY CONFUSED CODES: - Puma 2.4 TDCi: The direct predecessor (2007-2011). Externally similar, but the 2.2L features a revised turbo setup, different engine management to meet Euro 5 standards, and a revised 6-speed gearbox with different ratios. - 224DT: Land Rover's internal designation for the same 2.2L Duratorq engine when fitted to the Freelander 2 and Range Rover Evoque. While mechanically identical, the Defender application features unique mounting points, a different wiring loom, and specific ECU mapping, making a direct swap problematic without modifications. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Attempting to drop a Freelander 2-sourced 224DT into a Defender chassis without updating the ECU, wiring loom, and ancillary brackets will result in persistent fault codes, poor drivability, and potential sensor incompatibility. CLOSING LINE: Not 100% sure? Enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact Puma 2.2 TDCi fitment before any quotes are sent.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Puma 2.2 TDCi - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine is a viable option for budget-conscious rebuilds, provided it comes with a documented service history and recent compression test results. Given the engine's age and typical off-road use, the primary risk is hidden wear from oil starvation or neglected EGR and turbo maintenance. Explore our vetted used Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine is the most recommended choice for classic Defender restorations. A quality rebuild will systematically address age-related wear: a new or refurbished turbocharger, updated EGR cooler, fresh injector seals, and a timing chain tensioner refresh. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock and is the most cost-effective way to secure long-term peace of mind. Compare reconditioned Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples, vehicles that have suffered from overheating, or if the cylinder bores show measurable scoring. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, a reground crankshaft, and a complete refresh of the oil pump, ensuring the engine can reliably handle another 100,000+ miles of off-road or heavy-duty use. View rebuilt Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine specifications.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Buying through the EnginesMarket network means you can opt for a full supply and fit service, with the replacement engine installed by a Land Rover specialist and backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi is typically found in host vehicles (the final generation Defender 90/110/130) valued between £15,000 and £40,000+, heavily dependent on condition, mileage, and restoration quality. For standard, unmodified examples valued under £20,000, a £2,000+ reconditioned Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine replacement represents a significant but generally justifiable investment, given the classic status of the vehicle. However, for heavily degraded examples, we strongly advise evaluating the vehicle's overall condition and scrap value before committing to a full Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine replacement.

items.question: How much does a Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi engine typically costs between £2,000 and £3,500 for supply only. Fitted costs through an independent specialist will add approximately £650-£910 in labour. Used units are available from £800 but carry a higher risk of inherited wear.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Puma 2.2 TDCi?
items.answer: The most common failure is EGR cooler leaks, particularly between 80,000 and 150,000 miles. This can lead to unexplained coolant loss and potential engine overheating if ignored. Turbocharger actuator failure and timing chain tensioner wear are also well-documented issues.
bullets: This can lead to unexplained coolant loss and potential engine overheating if ignored.
Turbocharger actuator failure and timing chain tensioner wear are also well-documented issues.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the Puma 2.2 TDCi engine?
items.answer: The Puma 2.2 TDCi was fitted exclusively to the final generation of the classic Land Rover Defender (L316) between 2011 and 2016. It was introduced to meet Euro 5 emissions standards, replacing the earlier 2.4-litre Puma unit. It is the exact same engine fitted to contemporary Ford and Land Rover models as the 224DT.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Puma 2.2 TDCi engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of inherited EGR, turbo, and timing chain issues. A proper rebuild will systematically replace the known weak points, including the EGR cooler, turbo actuator, and timing chain tensioner. A used unit is only advisable if it comes with comprehensive, documented proof that these specific preventative repairs have already been completed.
